title: The Law of Reversibility: from a Mehedinți hamlet to a book printed in Lugoj and read nowhere
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Valea Hoțului, Mehedinți: born on three hectares
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja'; ro.wikipedia, same). The date is stable across every source consulted; the place-name is not. en.wikipedia gives Valea Izvorului, the Institutul Cultural Român profile gives Izvorul Aneștilor, local tradition gives Valea Hoțului. All three name the one settlement in Livezile commune, renamed Ștefan Odobleja in 2005. Coordinate taken from ro.wikipedia's article on the village itself, 44.57556, 22.83139; the afterlife lens of the research pool carried 44.73, 22.78 for the same place, which is wrong by about 18 km and is not used here.
stops.campa: A son is born to Ștefan and Maria Odobleja, peasants of Mehedinți, on a holding of some three hectares: arable, a vineyard, a pasture, an orchard. The hamlet carries three names in the record at once, Valea Hoțului in the mouths of its neighbours, Valea Izvorului on the maps, Izvorul Aneștilor in the church books. The Danube runs to the south of it, the Carpathian foothills close it off to the north, and the only road out is the road to Turnu Severin. The house keeps cattle, and the boy will be the one sent to watch them.

stops.name: The village school, Valea Hoțului: first in his class five years running
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only (ro.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja': primary school begun 1909 in his native village, finishing first each year). No month or day is given in any source consulted, so both default to 01. The teacher's name, N. T. Ismană, and the detail of reading in the fields with the cattle come from the research pool's family and commemorative sources, not from a source fetched directly.
stops.campa: He enters the village primary school under a teacher remembered as N. T. Ismană and finishes first in his class each of the five years. The reading is done in the fields, where he is sent out with the cattle and takes a book along. There is no library in the hamlet and no second teacher. What the school gives him is Romanian letters, arithmetic, and the habit of finishing first, which in a commune this size means being noticed by the one or two men in the county who can arrange for a peasant's son to go further than the fields.
suggested_refs: The primary school of Valea Hoțului under the teacher N. T. Ismană

stops.name: Liceul Traian, Turnu Severin: the French that made the later books possible
stops.date_confidence: institution attested, entry year inferred. Liceul Traian, now Colegiul Național Traian, founded 1 September 1883, is confirmed by ro.wikipedia, 'Drobeta-Turnu Severin', and is named as his secondary school by ro.wikipedia. Neither Romanian nor English Wikipedia gives 1914 as the year of entry; that year is an inference from his age and is used here only to order the segment. The teacher remembered as Chiricu, the Wilhelm Tell translations, and the year lost in 1916 come from the research pool's commemorative sources, not from a directly fetched source. The death of his brother Dumitru of typhus in 1917 is attested through the dedication of La Phonoscopie.
stops.campa: At about twelve he leaves the hamlet for the town on the Danube and enters Liceul Traian, founded in 1883, the secondary school of the whole county. A teacher remembered as Chiricu drills him in French through translation, Wilhelm Tell among the texts, and the language takes: three decades later he will write nine hundred pages in it. The war reaches the school in 1916 and, with family poverty, costs him a full year. His brother Dumitru dies of typhus in 1917.

The dedication of La Phonoscopie (1935) to his brother Dumitru

stops.name: Malovăț: the boy teaching before he has finished being taught
stops.date_confidence: attested to exact dates in the research pool from military-personnel-file testimony, 1 September 1921 to 1 September 1922, but that file was not fetched directly in this session and no independent record of the appointment was located. Coordinate corrected: ro.wikipedia, 'Malovăț, Mehedinți' gives 44°42'20"N 22°43'46"E, that is 44.70556, 22.72944, at 108 m elevation. The pool's geography lens carried 44.7167, 22.6167, about 9 km too far west.
stops.campa: Before his own studies are done he takes a post as substitute teacher at Malovăț, in the hill country north of Turnu Severin, from the first of September 1921 to the first of September 1922. It is money, and it is the only trade a half-educated peasant's son can practise legally. He is nineteen. The village has a school, a church, and a hundred metres of elevation over the Danube plain, and he teaches in it for exactly one year before the scholarship comes through.
suggested_refs: The village school of Malovăț, Mehedinți county

stops.name: Ada Kaleh: the Turkish island in the Danube
stops.date_confidence: attested in the research pool from military-file testimony to the span 1921-1922 without a month; the date here is an ordering device placing the island after the Malovăț appointment, and both month and day default to 01. Island coordinate and description from ro.wikipedia, 'Ada Kaleh', fetched. The teaching engagement itself rests on the pool's file testimony and was not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: In the same stretch of years he teaches on Ada Kaleh, an Ottoman island a mile and a half long in the middle of the Danube below Orșova, still Turkish in speech and custom long after the empire that put it there is gone: a mosque, an Austrian fortress, tobacco, rose gardens, some six hundred people. He crosses by boat to work. In 1970 the island will be drowned whole under the Iron Gates reservoir, and every room he taught in that year is now under water.

stops.name: Institutul Sanitar Militar, Bucharest: a peasant's son buys medicine with his years
stops.date_confidence: year attested (ro.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja': enrolment in medical studies in the military section, 1922); ministerial decision no. 927 and the role of the Severin schoolmaster Teodor Costescu come from the research pool's military-file research and were not independently confirmed. Month and day default to 01. Coordinate corrected: the pool gave 44.4346, 26.0696, which is the Faculty of Medicine in Cotroceni, not the Institute. The Institutul Medico-Militar is at Strada Institutul Medico-Militar 3-5 near Gara de Nord, 44.44522, 26.07271 (OSM Nominatim), about 1.2 km away.
stops.campa: By ministerial decision he enters the military sanitary institute in Bucharest as a scholarship student, on the advice of Teodor Costescu, the Severin schoolmaster who has made a practice of arranging such things for poor boys of the county. The terms are plain: the army pays for the medicine, and the physician belongs to the army afterwards. He will keep that side of the bargain for twenty-four years, through four garrison towns, a frontier post, and the Don. Bucharest is the first city he has lived in.

stops.name: The Faculty of Medicine, Bucharest: a thesis on people struck by cars
stops.date_confidence: the year and the thesis subject are attested (en.wikipedia and ro.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja': doctorate 1928, a medico-legal study of automobile accidents). The day is contested inside the research pool itself, 14 June in the personnel file against 13 June in the family archive; 14 June is used and the disagreement is not resolved. Venue corrected: the pool placed this at the Institutul de Medicină Legală Mina Minovici, which sits at 44.38938, 26.14314 some 5 km southeast; a medical doctorate was defended before the Faculty of Medicine, whose coordinate is 44.43429, 26.07144, and the medico-legal subject does not move the venue.
stops.campa: He defends Accidentele de automobil, studiu medico-legal, a forensic study of automobile accidents, and takes his doctorate in medicine and surgery with an average recorded at nine out of ten. The subject is new to the country. Bucharest in the 1920s is a city where the motorcar and the horse cart share one boulevard and the coroner has to establish which of them killed the man on the paving. It is his last examination as a student, and the army posts him within months.

stops.name: Regimentul de Pontonieri, Brăila: fogged mirrors and the law of the vicious circle
stops.date_confidence: posting attested (ro.wikipedia and the Institutul Cultural Român profile both list Brăila among his garrisons); the exact month of arrival and the evaluators' wording come from the research pool's reading of the personnel file and are not independently confirmed, so the month is a placement device. The 1929 publication is attested by the ICR profile, which dates Metoda de transonanță toracică to 1929 and describes it as the study announcing the law of reversibility; the pool's shorter title 'Metodă de transonanță' is corrected here.
stops.campa: His first posting is the pontoon regiment on the lower Danube at Brăila, engineers whose work is laying roadway across water. His superiors write that his theoretical grounding is wasted outside a hospital. He publishes small things: why the laryngoscope mirror fogs, how gravity can be turned to therapeutic use. In 1929 comes Metoda de transonanță toracică, a way of reading the chest by sound driven through it, and with it the first statement of the idea that governs all his later work: that effects run back into their causes.

stops.name: The 95th Infantry, Turnu Severin: the officer who does not come to the mess
stops.date_confidence: the transfer to Turnu Severin is attested as a garrison of his (ro.wikipedia); the precise instrument, High Decree no. 3304 of 10 October 1930, and the evaluators' remarks on his withdrawal from officer society come from the research pool's military-file reading, not independently verified. Coordinate is the municipal point of Drobeta-Turnu Severin, 44°37'24"N 22°40'04"E per ro.wikipedia; the barracks itself is not located.
stops.campa: By high decree he transfers, at his own request, to the infantry regiment at Turnu Severin, to be within reach of his family and the hamlet. The evaluations are consistent and faintly puzzled: orderly, intellectually cultivated, of exceptional medical culture, and absent from the officers' society. They put the withdrawal down to reading. What he is in fact assembling, out of physiology, physics, psychology and his own work on sound, is a single principle for which he does not yet have a word.

stops.name: Regimentul 17 Infanterie, Lugoj: the productive years
stops.date_confidence: Lugoj is attested as one of his garrisons by both ro.wikipedia and the Institutul Cultural Român profile; the detachment date of 15 April 1933 and the 1937 evaluation of the sanitary administration of some 1,900 men come from the research pool's military-file reading and were not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: Detached to Lugoj in the Banat, four hundred kilometres from the Danube hamlet, he stays for eight years. A 1937 evaluation records that a regiment of some nineteen hundred men under his sanitary administration kept an unusually low sick rate through the manoeuvres. The rest of his time goes to writing. Two books are being built at once in the same rooms, one on how to listen to a body, one on the general law he believes governs bodies, minds, machines and societies without distinction.

stops.name: Lugoj: La Phonoscopie, printed here and sold from Paris
stops.date_confidence: date corrected against a catalogue. The Bibliothèque nationale de France holds 'La Phonoscopie, nouvelle méthode d'exploration clinique, par le Dr St. Odobleja', dated 1935. en.wikipedia and ro.wikipedia both give 1932 for this title; the BnF record is preferred and the contradiction is recorded rather than argued. Month and day are not given anywhere and default to 01. The Medic General dr. Papiu Alexandru prize is attested for 1937 by en.wikipedia and by the ICR profile. Odobleja is not attested as having travelled to Paris at any point in his life; the Paris connection is a distributor's, and the stop is therefore placed at Lugoj, where the book was printed and where he was.
stops.campa: La Phonoscopie, nouvelle méthode d'exploration clinique appears: a clinical method for reading the sounds of the body's surface, written in French, printed in Lugoj, distributed out of Paris by Gaston Doin. He does not go to Paris, this year or ever. The book is dedicated to his brother Dumitru, dead of typhus in 1917. Two years later the army gives it the Medic General dr. Papiu Alexandru prize for military medical writing, the first official honour of his working life.
suggested_refs: Ștefan Odobleja, La Phonoscopie, nouvelle méthode d'exploration clinique (1935), BnF catalogue record

stops.name: The IX International Congress of Military Medicine and Pharmacy, Bucharest: a prospectus handed out
stops.date_confidence: the congress and his participation are attested (en.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja'); the dates of 8-12 June 1937, the title 'Démonstration de phonoscopie', the French prospectus, and the interest of William Seaman Bainbridge of the American naval medical delegation come from the research pool's family-archive and commemorative sources and are tagged there as reconstruction. Coordinate is a central Bucharest point; the congress venue was not located.
stops.campa: He presents Démonstration de phonoscopie before the ninth international congress of military medicine, and hands out to delegates from thirty armies a French prospectus announcing the book he has not yet finished printing. The head of the American naval medical delegation, William Seaman Bainbridge, is said to have taken particular interest. What became of the prospectuses is not known. No letter, no citation, no library accession has ever been produced linking a single one of them to anybody.

stops.name: The Auspitz printing house, Lugoj: sixty-five days of stopped presses
stops.date_confidence: documented in the research pool from the 1983 publication of the Odobleja personal archive in Revista Arhivelor, which gives the contract of 21 September 1937, the 35,000-lei advance, the run of 2,000 copies, roughly sixty-five lost working days, and the withdrawal of the suit on 24 October 1938. That publication was not fetched directly this session, so the whole episode rests on the pool's account of it.
stops.campa: He contracts with the Adolf Auspitz concern, run by Iosif Schlinger, for two thousand copies of Psychologie consonantiste, and pays thirty-five thousand lei in advance out of a regimental physician's salary. Paper runs short and the presses stand idle some sixty-five working days. He sues his own printer. On the twenty-fourth of October 1938 he withdraws the action, the printer having agreed to finish the book. The quarrel survives in full because he kept every paper of it.
suggested_refs: The Odobleja personal archive, published in Revista Arhivelor (1983)

stops.name: Lugoj: Psychologie consonantiste, volume one
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (en.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja': volume I 1938, Librairie Maloine of Paris, printed in Lugoj). No month is given and both month and day default to 01. The quotation is verified verbatim against the full text of Ștefan Iancu's article at archive.org item ifvol-2-nr-1-art.-5; note that Iancu gives no page reference inside Odobleja's own book, so the quotation is cited at one remove.
stops.campa: Volume one appears under the Paris imprint of Librairie Maloine, physically printed in the Banat town where he is stationed. Its claim is single and is applied without limit: that alongside straight-line causality there is a closed-loop kind, in which one phenomenon is by turns effect and cause, and that this circle governs physiology, psychology, physics, economics and society alike. He calls it the law of reversibility. The word cybernetics does not yet exist in the sense it will later carry.
stops.quote: Reversibility is a vicious circle between the cause and its effect. It is an oscillation between two states which alternatively induce themselves one another. Reciprocity of actions... Besides the acyclic causality there is a cyclic one, in a vicious circle. The same phenomenon is then one at a time effect and cause.
stops.quote_source: Ștefan Odobleja, Psychologie consonantiste (Librairie Maloine, Paris, vol. I 1938 / vol. II 1939; printed in Lugoj), quoted in Ștefan Iancu, 'Stefan Odobleja - The Main Romanian Forerunner of the Cybernetics,' Annals of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, Series on Science and Technology of Information 2, no. 1 (2009): 53
suggested_refs: Ștefan Odobleja, Psychologie consonantiste, vol. I (Librairie Maloine, 1938)
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja'
Ștefan Iancu, Annals of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, Series on Science and Technology of Information 2, no. 1 (2009), full text at archive.org item ifvol-2-nr-1-art.-5

stops.name: Lugoj: volume two, and the science of the sciences
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (en.wikipedia, 'Ștefan Odobleja'). The extent is given as nearly 900 pages by en.wikipedia and as 884 pages by the Institutul Cultural Român profile; both figures are carried here without adjudication, along with the figure of about 300 diagrams. Month and day default to 01. The quotation is verified verbatim against Iancu's full text, where it is introduced as the deepest definition Odobleja gives to ethics.
stops.campa: The second volume completes a work of some eight hundred and eighty-four pages by his own count, with about three hundred figures, written in French by a Romanian garrison doctor and addressed to nobody in particular. It proposes consonantist psychology as a science of the sciences, and it defines ethics inside the same closed-loop logic as everything else, as a matter of prevention and cure. Europe goes to war before the year is out. The book reaches a few reviewers. Then nothing.
stops.quote: Ethics is the science of the prophylaxis and therapeutics of the evil.
stops.quote_source: Ștefan Odobleja, Psychologie consonantiste, quoted in Ștefan Iancu, 'Stefan Odobleja - The Main Romanian Forerunner of the Cybernetics,' Annals of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, Series on Science and Technology of Information 2, no. 1 (2009): 54

stops.name: Lipcani, Hotin: the frontier post
stops.date_confidence: the transfer to the 4th Rifles at Lipcani, Hotin county, effective 1 April 1938, comes from the research pool's reading of the military personnel file. The claim that the move was disciplinary and that he was suspected of communist or materialist sympathies rests on Odobleja's own 1978 interview, reported in the pool; no Siguranța file confirming it has been produced, and this is recorded as unresolved rather than as fact.
stops.campa: While volume one is still on the presses he is transferred to a rifle regiment at Lipcani, on the Prut in northern Bessarabia, about as far from Lugoj as the kingdom can send a man. Forty years later he will say the move was punishment, made while he was under suspicion of communist or materialist sympathies. No file confirming that has surfaced. In June 1940 the Soviet Union takes Bessarabia and Bukovina by ultimatum, and the regiment walks out of the province it was posted to hold.
suggested_refs: Lipcani on the Prut, Hotin county, Bessarabia, before the Soviet ultimatum of June 1940
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file and Odobleja's 1978 interview

stops.name: Grupul 4 Vânători Moto, Turda: chief physician
stops.date_confidence: posting dated 1 May 1940 in the research pool's reading of the military personnel file, with the superior's note on his exceptional medical culture from the same source; not independently confirmed. The Second Vienna Award of 30 August 1940, which moved the Hungarian border to within a few kilometres of Turda, is general history and is not in dispute.
stops.campa: His regiment dissolved, he becomes chief physician of a motorised rifle group at Turda in Transylvania. A superior writes that his medical culture is exceptional. Within four months the Second Vienna Award hands northern Transylvania to Hungary and the frontier runs a few kilometres from the town. The two French volumes travel with him in a trunk, unread by anybody in the garrison. He is thirty-seven. He treats soldiers, requisitions supplies, files his reports.
suggested_refs: The 4th Motorised Rifles at Turda, 1940, and the Second Vienna Award border
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file

stops.name: Regimentul 36 Infanterie, Cernavodă: the bridge before the war
stops.date_confidence: transfer dated 25 May 1941 in the research pool's reading of the military personnel file, as physician of the first battalion; not independently confirmed. Romania's entry into the invasion of the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 is general history. The characterisation of the Saligny bridge as the rail link to Constanța is geography, not a claim from the file.
stops.campa: He is posted to Cernavodă on the Danube, where the Saligny bridge carries the railway east to Constanța and the port, as physician of the first battalion. It is his third posting in three years. He examines the men and passes them fit. Four weeks later, on the twenty-second of June 1941, Romania enters the invasion of the Soviet Union alongside Germany, and the battalion he has been keeping healthy marches east across the same Prut he was garrisoned on three years before.
suggested_refs: The Saligny bridge at Cernavodă, and the 36th Infantry Regiment, 1941
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file

stops.name: The bend of the Don: a dugout with twenty wounded in it
stops.date_confidence: the improvised dugout aid station sheltering around twenty wounded, and the evacuation work singled out for praise, come from the research pool's reading of the military personnel file and are tagged there as reconstruction. Only the year 1942 is given, so month and day default to 01. The coordinate is an approximation to the Don Bend sector; the exact village is not resolved in any source consulted.
stops.campa: East of everything, in the great bend of the Don, he digs an aid station into the ground and holds some twenty wounded men in it while organising their evacuation from the forward line. The personnel file singles the work out for praise. The theory of the closed loop is four years old and is in a trunk in Romania. Here the loop runs shell, wound, sledge, dugout, and the men who can be moved go west while the line holds. It holds until the nineteenth of November.
suggested_refs: The Romanian Third Army sector on the Don bend, autumn 1942
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file

stops.name: Varlamov, Derșam, Vislogubova: the line breaks
stops.date_confidence: the date of Operation Uranus, 19 November 1942, is general history. His separation from the regiment and the route through Varlamov (given as Varlamar in one reading), Derșam and the fighting around Vislogubova toward Kamenka come from the research pool's reading of the military personnel file. None of these small Don-region localities could be independently located, so the coordinate repeats the sector approximation of the previous stop.
stops.campa: Operation Uranus opens on the nineteenth of November and the Romanian front on the Don is through inside a day. He is separated from his regiment and carried along in the collapse, through Varlamov, through Derșam, through fighting around Vislogubova, toward Kamenka. None of these places can now be fixed on a map with confidence; the file names them and the war moved the names. He is forty years old, on foot, in a Russian November, without his unit.
suggested_refs: The collapse of the Romanian Third Army in Operation Uranus, 19 November 1942
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file

stops.name: Odessa: frostbitten, and entered as dead
stops.date_confidence: attested in the research pool from the military personnel file and Odobleja's own later recollection to the span late 1942 to early 1943; no exact date is given, so month and day default to 01. The detail that his own unit at Cernavodă had listed him dead or missing, and that later retellings compress this into 'declared dead at Stalingrad', is carried from the pool as its account of the file.
stops.campa: Frostbitten in the retreat, he is taken into a field hospital and then evacuated to the interior-zone hospital at Odessa, in the city Romania is administering as the capital of Transnistria. When he reaches Cernavodă again he learns that his own regiment had entered him as dead or missing. Later retellings compress this into a single sentence, that he was declared dead at Stalingrad. What the file records is a frostbitten officer returning to a unit that had written him off, and going back on duty.
suggested_refs: The Romanian interior-zone evacuation hospital at Odessa, 1942-1943
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file and Odobleja's later recollection

stops.name: Ambulanța 37 Munte: westward with the army that changed sides
stops.date_confidence: the depot service in Bucharest in 1944, the promotion to major, and the attachment to a mountain field-ambulance unit for the westward campaign come from the research pool's reading of the military personnel file. The coup of 23 August 1944 is general history. No month is attested for the ambulance posting, so the date is a placement device; the coordinate is an approximation along the Transylvanian campaign route rather than a located place.
stops.campa: After a spell at an equipment depot in the capital and his promotion to major, the coup of the twenty-third of August 1944 turns Romania around, and he goes west at forty-two with a mountain field ambulance as Romanian troops fight German and Hungarian forces back through Transylvania. The war ends for him there. His role in it is medical from the first day to the last, and nothing in any file ties him to a combat command, to a court, or to the political police.
suggested_refs: Ambulanța 37 Munte in the Romanian westward campaign, autumn 1944
sources: research pool, citing the military personnel file

stops.name: Cercul Teritorial Someș, near Cluj: the last posting, and a marriage
stops.date_confidence: the retirement from active service in 1946 is attested by en.wikipedia. The specifics, the Someș territorial circle around Dej and Cluj, the promotion to lieutenant-colonel of 8 May 1946, and the placement in the available cadre by High Decree no. 2269 of 22 July 1946, come from the research pool's reading of the military personnel file. The marriage is recorded in the family compilation without the wife's name; the pool notes a contradiction it does not resolve, three children in the family compilation against two, one of whom died, in a 2018 press account.
stops.campa: His final posting attaches him to the Someș territorial circle around Dej and Cluj, and the last evaluation is favourable. In the spring he marries a woman of the district whose name the surviving family compilation does not record. On the eighth of May he is promoted lieutenant-colonel; on the twenty-second of July, by high decree and at his own request, he is placed in the available cadre after some eighteen years of active service. He is forty-three, and out of the army.

stops.name: Valea Hoțului: the stamp is withdrawn
stops.date_confidence: the return to the native village and the withdrawal of his medical stamp come from the research pool, citing the military personnel file and a later military commemorative article; the pool records explicitly that the authority behind the withdrawal is not recovered. No month is attested, so the date is a placement device following the 22 July discharge. The unpaid treatment of villagers comes from the pool's family and commemorative sources.
stops.campa: He goes back to the hamlet. His medical stamp is taken from him, by whose authority the record does not say, and a country doctor without a stamp is a man who may not sign a prescription. He has twenty-four years of army service behind him and a doctorate the state will not let him use. He treats the poor of the villages anyway, off the books and for nothing. The two French volumes printed at Lugoj sit in a house where nobody for many kilometres reads French.
suggested_refs: The Odobleja house at Valea Hoțului after 1946

stops.name: Valea Hoțului: fifty thousand pages
